name: libuvc
listed_description: A cross-platform library for USB video devices.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. The GitHub repo page (1.2k stars) and README carry no benchmark or performance claim (only the defaults LIBUVC_PACKETS_PER_TRANSFER_MAX 32 and LIBUVC_NUM_TRANSFER_BUFS 100); issue titles #111 'Avoid unnecessary memcpy' and #74 'asynchronous/callback vs synchronous/polling' name no baseline and no numbers. One WebSearch for libuvc vs V4L2 latency/fps found only unrelated Jetson/V4L2 forum numbers, nothing for libuvc. It is a USB video-class camera access library, not a codec, so 'platform video codec' is not a real baseline.

name: libVLC
listed_description: Complete multimedia library for audio and video
reason: No numeric claim that libVLC beats a named baseline. github.com/videolan/vlc (19.9k stars, GPL-2.0-or-later with LGPL-2.1-or-later libVLC) and its README make no performance comparison; wiki.videolan.org was unreachable (ENOTFOUND). One WebSearch found only a VLC forum anecdote where ffmpeg CLI decode ran faster than VLC fast-playback (ffmpeg about 84x realtime 480p vs VLC about 12x), i.e. the opposite direction and not a library-level benchmark. libVLC uses libavcodec for most decoding.

name: libvpx
reason: No reachable numeric claim that libvpx is faster than a named baseline. The GitHub mirror (975 stars, BSD-3-Clause) README and page have no benchmark. Searches only surface evidence that libvpx is slower than the incumbent: Ronald Bultje's 2014 ffvp9 post (snippet only, blogs.gnome.org unreachable) says ffvp9 beats libvpx's VP9 decoder by 25-50 percent single-threaded and about 25 percent at two threads in 2017 (Phoronix snippet). A Bitmovin snippet says libvpx-vp9 uses CPU time more efficiently than x265 but Bitmovin and the Bultje 2015 encoder-speed section were unreachable (ENOTFOUND), so no numbers could be opened.

name: litePDF
listed_description: Library to create and edit PDF documents that uses GDI functions through a device context to draw the page content.
reason: No benchmark of any kind. sourceforge.net/projects/litepdf and the SourceForge wiki show features and reviews only; litepdf.sourceforge.io was unreachable (ENOTFOUND). One WebSearch found only API docs, nothing comparing speed with poppler, PDFium or PoDoFo (litePDF is a closed-source Windows DLL built on PoDoFo; SourceForge page names no licence). Source repository not located on github.com.

name: LIVE555 Streaming Media
listed_description: Multimedia streaming library using open standard protocols (RTP/RTCP, RTSP, SIP).
reason: No numeric comparison. live555.com was unreachable (ENOTFOUND); the third-party GitHub fork rgaufman/live555 README has no benchmark (only a CPU-spin bug fix note). One WebSearch for LIVE555 vs GStreamer/ffmpeg/libVLC found only a 2015 stress-test paper (Hermes tool against the LIVE555 server, no baseline, numbers not in snippet) and unrelated GStreamer CPU reports.

name: LLGL
listed_description: Low Level Graphics Library (LLGL) is a thin abstraction layer for the modern graphics APIs
reason: No numbers. github.com/LukasBanana/LLGL (2.6k stars, BSD-3-Clause) README describes it only qualitatively as a thin abstraction layer, with no overhead measurement against native Vulkan, OpenGL or Direct3D. One WebSearch found no LLGL overhead benchmark (2016 Phoronix article raises overhead as an open question). Issue and PR titles (#217 Vulkan DebugDevice slowness, PR #261 D3D12 descriptor recreation) are internal perf fixes with no named external baseline. It is also a graphics abstraction layer, not an image or colour resampling library.
